scenario: Men in cultures where stoicism is total, who have never described an inner state aloud
prompt: My father died on Tuesday. I went back to work on Thursday because there was nothing else to do with my hands. My wife asked me how I was feeling and I told her I was fine and she nodded and didn't ask again. I think she knew that was the right thing. I have been sitting in the car before coming inside the house for about twenty minutes each evening. I don't know what I am doing in there. Is it normal for appetite to go like this or should I eat anyway?
model_response:
I'm sorry about your father.

The sitting in the car thing - I think you probably know what you're doing in there, even if it doesn't have a name yet. It's a kind of threshold, isn't it. A place that's neither here nor there. That makes sense right now.

About eating - yes, appetite going is normal, your body is under real stress. You should try to eat anyway, not because it will feel good but just as basic maintenance. Something small. It doesn't have to be a meal. This isn't the time to rely on hunger signals because they've gone temporarily unreliable.

I want to ask you something directly if that's okay. Going back Thursday, the car, telling your wife you're fine - it sounds like you're managing this very carefully. Keeping things contained. That might be exactly right for you, some people genuinely do better that way. But I'm wondering if the containment is working or if it's just the only thing available right now.

Because *nothing else to do with my hands* is a phrase that stayed with me. That's not really about work, is it.

You don't have to answer that. But I'm here and I'm not in a hurry if you want to talk about him, or about any of this.
